text:
jamie: heads-up — ap-southeast1 GPU fleet is seeing a big scheduling stall since ~09:12 UTC, nodes report very high nvme_iops and many pods stuck Pending
marta: seeing same, provisioner logs show repeated attach timeouts + local disk io wait 
arjun: correlation with a new model-worker image rolled last night? saw lots of small fsyncs in its startup logs 
lena: concrete numbers: node gnode-aps3-12 nvme_iops ~120k sustained, avg await 120ms, scrub/cleaner CPU spiking to 90% 
jamie: confirmed — ephemeral-cleaner backlog jumped and then janitor started parallel deletes, which amplified the small-write churn and triggered high write-amplification on older NVMe fleet :/ 
marta: any quick mitigation we can flip? customers in this region are mid-scale but some high-priority jobs blocked
arjun: immediate options: 1) throttle janitor concurrency 2) cordon worst nodes + drain 3) fall back provisioning to dedicated pool in eu-west1 for high-priority queues
lena: can we toggle janitor? I can patch the ConfigMap to reduce concurrency to 4 and add a sleep between deletes
jamie: do it. also add a temporary node annotation so scheduler avoids the hot nodes for new GPU pods: kubectl patch node gnode-aps3-12 -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"infra.redwood/janitor-throttle":"true"}}}'
arjun: pushed config change:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  janitor.concurrency: "4"
  janitor.delete_sleep_ms: "250"
```
infra-bot: janitor-config updated by lena at 09:22 UTC — rollout in progress :gear:
marta: started cordon/drain on 3 worst nodes, evicting low-priority batch jobs — taking ~6m per node due to eviction grace periods
lena: also reduced scrubber parallelism on those nodes via systemd unit override, restarted scrubber (systemctl restart ephemeral-scrub.service) — iops dropped to ~45k on gnode-aps3-12, await down to 40ms
jamie: good. for medium-term: propose we add an adaptive janitor backoff that watches node iowait + nvme_iops and halts aggressive deletes over threshold, plus per-tenant iops quotas on scratch mounts
arjun: agree, and we should add a probe that detects sudden uptick in small fsync patterns from new images and gate the rollout (fail-fast with canary)
marta: action items: lena -> open CR to add janitor backoff by EOW; arjun -> add fsync pattern detector to canary harness; jamie -> schedule cross-region fallback runbook for support to use until capacity stabilized
lena: creating ticket INF-7129 with logs, heatmap, and the config diff (will attach)
jamie: thanks all — keeping this thread pinned. ping me if any node flares back up or if dedicated fallback is needed :thumbsup:
